text:
rita: Morning! On my first day and hitting a few blockers getting dev env set up on an M2 Mac. asdf plugin-add fails intermittently with TLS errors, and when node does install the asdf shim isn't being picked up by VS Code tasks. Any quick wins? :wave:

owen: Welcome rita! A couple of quick checks: 1) ensure asdf is installed via Homebrew or git in ~/.asdf, 2) put `eval "$(asdf init -)"` near the top of your shell rc (zprofile/zshrc depending on login vs interactive), 3) check PATH order with `echo $PATH` so ~/.asdf/shims comes first.

kate: For the TLS hiccups on M-series macs, we usually see corporate TLS interception (corp MITM) or old curl/libressl in PATH. Confirm `which curl` is /usr/bin/curl or brew's curl, and if corp proxy is present add the corp CA to the system keychain: `sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain ~/Downloads/corp.crt`. Restart shells after.

rita: I do have the corp VPN and a PAC file. I tried adding the CA but `asdf plugin-add nodejs` still times out sometimes.

owen: If you use a PAC, run a local proxy like cntlm or tinyproxy and point HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY to it. Some asdf plugins spawn git/curl without inheriting GUI envs so export both uppercase and lowercase vars in zprofile and zshrc. Also try `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=false git -c http.sslCAInfo=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt clone ...` only if you understand the security tradeoffs (prefer adding CA).

kate: VS Code tasks: the integrated terminal may not load zprofile. Launching VS Code from terminal (`code .`) ensures it inherits your environment. For tasks specifically, set "options": { "shell": { "executable": "/bin/zsh", "args": ["-l", "-i"] } } in .vscode/tasks.json so commands run in a login interactive shell and pick up asdf shims.

rita: ah that explains the mismatch. I also noticed my dotfiles bootstrap created a ~/.local.env but it's empty. Should I add tokens there?

owen: Keep secrets out of repo — we use 1Password. Install op CLI and fetch tokens into ~/.local.env locally if needed, but make sure the file is in .gitignore. Example: `eval $(op signin) && op item get "redwood/dev-tokens" --fields token > ~/.local.env` (read docs first). We prefer direnv for loading local.env safely: `.envrc` contains `source_env ~/.local.env` and you `direnv allow` to enable.

kate: One more gotcha: brew-installed node might shadow asdf. Run `brew unlink node` or `brew uninstall node` if you want asdf-managed node to take precedence. After that open a fresh shell and run `asdf global nodejs <version>` and `which node` should point at ~/.asdf/shims/node.

rita: my `which node` still shows /usr/local/bin/node even after unlinking; PATH seems cached somewhere.

owen: Check launch agents for GUI apps. On mac, GUI apps launched via Spotlight/Finder don't inherit shell env. That's why putting exports in ~/.zprofile and launching VS Code from terminal helps. Also check you don't have a custom /etc/paths.d file adding /usr/local/bin earlier. `echo $PATH | tr ':' '
'` helps debug order.

kate: If you're comfortable, run `asdf reshim nodejs` after install. That regenerates shims. Lastly, for gpg-related errors when installing node via asdf-nodejs, ensure gnupg is installed (`brew install gnupg`) and run the plugin's key import script `~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`.

rita: Thanks — I'll try restarting VS Code from terminal, check PATH order, and use direnv+1Password for tokens. Anything else specific to Apple Silicon?

owen: On Apple Silicon, some build deps for python/ruby/node need `arch -arm64 brew install ...` or Rosetta variants. If a build fails, check the plugin docs for necessary libs (openssl, readline). We have a short KB page in onboarding about common arm64 tweaks.

kate: infra-bot note: onboarding KB updated with "mac M1/M2 asdf & VS Code tips" and sample tasks.json snippet: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboarding/macos-asdf-vscode :page_with_curl:

rita: great, thanks all — will report back if anything else pops up. :pray:
